comment: SCOPE BARRIERS + REFERENCE RESOLUTION. `<template>` content is an inert fragment and `<slot>` content is light-DOM fallback; neither is rendered where it is written. An ADDRESSABLE barrier owns its own fragment; a BARE one does not, and its named descendants belong to the nearest live ancestor carrying `inTemplateBarrier`. A template id and its live-DOM twin are two nodes in two trees and must never share a name. A `<label for>` may name a control declared LATER — legal HTML, and the pre-fix map only resolved backward references, so a forward label silently emitted nothing.

expectRelationships.comment: An addressable barrier owns its own fragment.
A BARE barrier is not a node: its fragment's element belongs to the nearest live ancestor, and the DOM tree the browser builds agrees.
Two trees, two nodes, two names.

FORWARD reference: the label is on line 41 and its control on 42. SOURCE is the element that WRITES the reference (`lbl-later`, which carries an id), not the nearest named ancestor — this file pinned `from: app` until 2026-10-12, when the lane's own F5 oracle was measured on the same document: `deriveHtmlEdges` derives `uses lbl-later -> declared-below`, so the old pin ratified a divergence from the lane's own truth. Re-pinned FIRST, then the analyzer's label branch was fixed (it was the only one of the four in-document reference emitters sourcing `frame.nearestNamed`; the resource carriers, the IDREF class and the fragment href all source `currentId`).
BACKWARD reference behaves identically — and names its own actor for the same reason.
An ambiguous id resolves to the FIRST, as getElementById does, and says so. The oracle agrees on the actor here too (`uses lbl-twin -> twin`).

forbidRelationships.comment: A fragment's element is not a child of the element that encloses the barrier in the source.
The ambiguous id resolves to the FIRST for REFERENCES. (The second element is still contained by `app` — it is a real node in the live tree — so only the reference is forbidden, not the containment.)
A label pointing at an id that does not exist is not a reference. Silence here is the honest answer, not a gap.
